newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK confident staying tourism mecca with China rule.
newsitem.headline: HK confident staying tourism mecca with China rule.

text.p: Looming Chinese rule over Hong Kong will not scare away tourists, and the territory will remain a mecca for travellers, a senior tourism official said.

Tourist authorities are launching a "Hong Kong 100 Days of Wonder" programme to promote the city from July 1, after Britain hands its colony back to China, said Kent Hayden-Sadler, deputy executive director of the Hong Kong Tourist Association.
The long programme will extend handover celebrations for an expected 100,000 visitors arriving daily, he said.
"We are confident and expect to receive over a million visitors in July and August," he said.
Chairman of the Hong Kong Hotels Association, Thomas Axmacher, said that 8,000 hotel rooms, which had stood vacant around May, had now fallen to about 6,000.

Hotels had jacked up room prices, some by as much as 60 percent, some months before the handover, expecting a surge of visitors around the historic changeover next Monday, but the high prices scared away would-be visitors.
Axemacher estimated that still vacant hotel rooms will be taken up around the July 1 handover, now five days away.
Hayden-Sadler said he was confident Hong Kong's attraction for tourists will not fade under Chinese rule.
"Hong Kong has been working together with China in tourism development and tourist promotion for a number of years. We complement each other well," Hayden-Sadler said.
"Visitors are looking to have a holiday of a lifetime in China. We are making sure that Hong Kong is perceived as one of the major attractions of China." he said.
